scene: A cartoon man with short brown hair, half-closed eyelids and a closed smile stands at left in a patched brown sweater and patched, torn blue jeans. Behind his hip hangs a worn brown briefcase stuffed with banknote bundles that carry a green glow at the far left edge. A black curved arrow below the headline points down-left toward him.
composition: The head and torso fill the left 40 percent of the frame and the two-line headline fills the right 55 percent, with a large empty white gap under the text. The arrow crosses that gap and links the words to the figure; the cash briefcase sits low at the extreme left edge, half hidden behind his body.
typography: Four black condensed words in two lines, with BROKE and RICH set larger than LOOK and GET; BROKE and RICH are the two highest-contrast shapes in the frame and stay sharp at 160x90. The text compresses the title's idea into a command and drops its 'stop trying' framing.
colors: Pure white background, black type and black outlines, with the pink skin, brown sweater and blue jeans as the only mid-tone colours. The neon-green glow around the banknotes is the single saturated accent and it is placed at the edge, away from the face.
psychology: Half-lidded eyes and a closed, slightly raised smile read as relaxed and knowing, and the patched sweater signals poverty. The face carries no fear or urgency, so the curiosity comes from the clothing-versus-cash mismatch.
partnership: The title is about the change that follows when someone stops trying to look rich; the thumbnail swaps that for a direct paradox, look broke and get rich. It adds the concrete cash-briefcase image but leaves the 'why' open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: BROKE and RICH first, then the man's face, then the patched sweater, and last the arrow and the green-glowing money at the left edge.
art: Clean outlined cartoon with flat shading and a soft grey floor shadow under the shoes, set on white so the cutout reads cleanly. The green glow on the notes is a digital effect that does not match the flat shading of the rest of the figure, and the briefcase is partly hidden by the body.
strength: The patched sweater beside the cash-stuffed briefcase puts the poor-versus-rich paradox in one glance.
weakness: The cash is the story's payoff but it is pushed to the far left edge and partly hidden, so the arrow points at the man rather than at the money.
bottleneck: The arrow's target is ambiguous: it lands on the shirt and not on the glowing cash, so the evidence for 'get rich' is the weakest-placed element.
action: Hypothesis: redirect the arrow to the money-filled briefcase and enlarge the briefcase to test whether pointing at the payoff reads faster than pointing at the figure.
mechanism: The patched clothing sits against a briefcase of glowing cash, so the picture holds the poor-looking-but-rich contradiction that the headline states in four words.
counterexample: Seq 15 uses the same cartoon character and arrow template but puts the money under the headline arrow, so its payoff object gets the arrow's attention.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon older man at left with swept grey hair, a grey beard and round glasses stands in a green knit sweater and brown corduroy trousers, one hand at his chin and his mouth slightly open. His other hand holds an open brown wallet with one banknote showing, and three coins fall out beneath it. A red curved arrow from the word CURVE sweeps back toward the falling coins.
composition: The figure occupies the left third at full height and the three-line text block fills the right two thirds, each line wider than the one above it. The red arrow is the only link across the white gap, and the wallet and coins sit at mid-height, below the figure's face.
typography: Three very large black capitals stacked on three lines, all fully legible at 160x90; CURVE is the tallest line and RETIREMENT the widest. The words repeat three of the title's terms and leave out '3 points' and 'smiling'.
colors: White background with black type; the muted green sweater and brown trousers are the figure's only colours, and the red arrow is the one saturated accent. The red arrow stands out more than anything else in the frame except the black headline.
psychology: Eyes glancing down toward the wallet, a hand at the chin and a small open mouth read as puzzled or concerned. Falling coins add a sense of money leaking out, and the grey beard marks him as an older person.
partnership: The headline echoes the title's key phrase almost word for word, so the text adds nothing beyond it. The falling coins imply spending that shrinks, which the title's 'smiling curve' does not say, leaving the actual curve shape to the video.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the word CURVE and the red arrow first, then the man's face and chin-hand pose, then the open wallet and coins, and finally RETIREMENT at the top.
art: Outlined cartoon with soft shading on the sweater and trousers, cleanly cut out on white. Wallet, coins and glasses are coherent and legible; the figure is relatively small and narrow, which leaves the right side to text.
strength: Three huge black words give an instantly legible topic label that survives any size.
weakness: The coins falling from the wallet suggest running out of money, which does not match a curve that, per the title, also rises, and it adds no visual of a curve.
bottleneck: No curve or chart appears anywhere, so the headline's key word has nothing visual behind it.
action: Hypothesis: replace the falling coins with a simple U-shaped curve drawn behind the man to test whether showing the curve beats the wallet metaphor.
mechanism: A man staring down at coins dropping from his wallet gives the dry word 'curve' a human cost image, while the three-word block names the subject in plain terms.
mechanism_secondary: topic label with concerned older figure
counterexample: Seq 19 puts an actual falling price chart beside its headline, giving the data object that this frame never shows.
expression_label: downward glance, hand on chin, mouth slightly open
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A stick-limbed cartoon man with spiky black hair, rectangular black sunglasses and a wide grin stands on boarding stairs at the open door of a large gold aeroplane. He wears a green textured tuxedo jacket, white shirt and green bow tie, with thin black arms and legs, and his hand grips the rail. A red curved arrow from the top-centre points left toward his head, and a gold turbofan engine and blue sky show behind the text.
composition: The figure stands left of centre at about two thirds of the frame height, and the gold fuselage fills the whole background. The two-line red headline sits at upper right, and the arrow runs from the text to the figure's head, giving a clear left-pointing path.
typography: Two words in red capitals with a thick black outline, the second word wider than the first, so they read clearly on the gold-and-blue ground at 160x90. The text names only the character and omits the title's money question and the $1 Billion figure.
colors: A dominant gold with warm highlights covers most of the frame, set against a blue sky strip and the red-and-black lettering. The green jacket and bow tie are the only cool accent on the figure and keep his silhouette against the gold.
psychology: A visible grin, sunglasses and rail grip suggest a relaxed visual presentation. The gold aircraft supplies a luxury cue; confidence or pleasure cannot be established as personal traits.
partnership: The title asks how fast a time traveler could earn $1 billion; the thumbnail answers with a visible sign of wealth but does not mention the sum. The gold jet adds an outcome and a question, how he got it, that the title does not show.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red TIME TRAVELER lettering first, then the arrow down to the grinning figure, then the gold jet behind him.
art: Digitally painted glossy gold plane with soft smears and highlights beside a thin-limbed flat cartoon figure; the two rendering styles differ, and the plane is blurrier than the outlined figure. The large gold shape lacks fine detail, so little is lost at small size.
strength: A grinning figure in sunglasses on a gold private jet communicates sudden wealth with no explanation.
weakness: The red text and gold plane compete for the top half, and the figure is thin and small against the huge fuselage.
bottleneck: The 'time' idea has no visual cue, since nothing in the frame signals a different era or a clock.
action: Hypothesis: add one anachronism, such as a clock or a period-dress detail in the doorway, to test whether a time cue makes the 'traveler' label visually earn its place.
mechanism: A grinning man in sunglasses stepping off a gold jet is a wealth image, and the red 'TIME TRAVELER' label tells the viewer which character is the traveler.
mechanism_secondary: luxury cue (gold jet) for an implied outcome
counterexample: Seq 24 uses a dotted arrow across a cliff gap to show a concrete journey, while this frame has no visible time cue.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A tall portrait-format image sits between two dusty-rose bars, so only the middle strip holds drawing. In it a stick figure with a featureless oval head holds a long black pole upward, with a wire running from the pole to a small box with a lightning symbol and on to an open box at lower right, where a white lightning bolt hits and sends black fragments upward. A thought bubble at upper left contains a bolt sketch, an equals sign and a small bolt symbol with scribbled red marks.
composition: Content occupies only the central strip, about a third of the frame width, and the two flat rose bars at each side take the rest. Inside the strip the figure is at left, the bolt at upper right and the box at the bottom right, forming a diagonal from the thought bubble to the strike point.
typography: No headline is visible. The only marks that look like writing are a few scribbled red strokes in the thought bubble, which are not readable at any size, so nothing in the image states the topic.
colors: Grey gradient behind black line art, with a bright white bolt as the only high-contrast element. The two side bars are a muted maroon-rose with no relationship to the artwork.
psychology: The figure has no facial features, so the image carries no expression; the interest comes from the bolt, the debris and the figure's upright posture. The scene is neutral in tone and there is no danger colour.
partnership: The title asks whether lightning power can be harvested, and the drawing shows exactly that setup with a rod, a wire and a bolt, so it illustrates the question but does not hint at the answer. The thought-bubble equation is unreadable.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white lightning bolt first, then the stick figure with the pole, then the thought bubble, and last the small box beneath the strike.
art: Thin hand-drawn line figure on a grainy grey gradient, with a brighter white rendered bolt that looks more detailed than the line art. The artwork is clean, but it occupies a narrow strip with large dead margins on both sides.
strength: The branching white bolt striking a box is the one high-contrast shape and tells the electricity story visually.
weakness: About two thirds of the frame is flat rose bars, and the actual drawing is tiny with fine line detail.
bottleneck: At 160x90 the figure and thought bubble shrink to specks, so only the bolt and the grey strip remain readable.
action: Hypothesis: re-crop the artwork into a full-width 16:9 frame with the bolt enlarged to test whether the dead margins are costing visibility.
mechanism: A stick figure rigged to a wire and a box beside a branching white bolt acts out the title's question as a diagram, with no words to carry it.
mechanism_secondary: diagram of the question with no text
counterexample: Seq 11 fills the whole frame with a big headline and two animals, so every element is large where this frame's drawing is tiny.
hero_object: white lightning bolt striking a box
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: WHY ONLY FROG LEGS? / EAT THIS / NOT THIS?
scene: A stick figure with a large round head, wide eyes, a finger at its nose and a drool drip stands in the middle with blue sweat drops and a red question mark beside it. Its other hand points left toward a grey plate of golden fried frog legs with yellow sparkle lines. At right a second plate holds a whole green frog with large round eyes, an X-shaped mouth and a blue tear.
composition: A yellow headline spans the whole top edge, the stick figure sits in the exact centre as a divider, and the two plates mirror each other left and right. The labels EAT THIS and NOT THIS? sit in the bottom corners, forming a symmetric top-middle-bottom layout.
typography: Eight words across three blocks: a four-word yellow headline with black outline at top, and two bottom labels, EAT THIS in green and NOT THIS? in red. All three remain readable at 160x90, with the headline strongest.
colors: Bright yellow, green, red and orange on a white ground, with grey plates and a light-blue sweat drop accent. Green and red mark the accepted and the rejected dish, so colour also carries the comparison.
psychology: Wide eyes, a drool drip, a sweat drop and a question mark on the central figure read as hunger mixed with confusion. The frog's X mouth and single tear add a pitiful tone that sets up the contrast.
partnership: The headline is nearly the title's question; the image adds the whole-frog counterpart and the eat-this-not-this split, which the title does not show. It frames the question as a puzzle about why one part is food and the rest is not.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow headline first, then the stick figure's face in the middle, then the fried legs at left, then the frog and NOT THIS? at right.
art: Flat cartoon with a consistent line weight and cartoon gloss, plus sparkles on the fried legs. The stick figure, frog and food are coherent, and the plates are clean shapes against white.
strength: The split of cooked legs versus a whole teary frog turns one phrase into a two-option picture.
weakness: Three text blocks plus a busy central figure with drool, sweat and a question mark add up to many small accents around the middle.
bottleneck: The central figure's drool, sweat drops and question mark crowd the middle and compete with the plates for first attention.
action: Hypothesis: remove the sweat drops and the drool so that only the question mark remains around the figure, to test whether a calmer centre lets the two plates carry the contrast.
mechanism: Two plates, one with cooked legs and one with a whole crying frog, make the title's 'why only legs' question a visible choice between two foods.
counterexample: Seq 10 shows one large object, a rifle, with a two-word headline, which is simpler than this three-block layout.
expression_label: wide eyes, drooling, finger at nose
hero_object: fried frog legs beside a whole frog
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: 4 TYPES OF / MEDICATIONS / TO AVOID / TO IMPROVE / MEMORY
scene: At right, a rounded-corner photo shows a woman with dark curly hair pulled back, small gold drop earrings and a beaded necklace. She wears a maroon blouse under a white coat with a stethoscope around her neck, and she gives a closed-mouth smile while looking toward the camera. A teal background fills the rest, and the text is on the left.
composition: Text occupies the left 55 percent in five lines and the photo panel the right 35 percent, with a larger gap between the third and fourth lines than between the others. Her face sits near the panel's upper centre, and the rounded corners separate the photo from the teal ground.
typography: Five lines in alternating black and white capitals, with AVOID and MEMORY in white and the others in black. The first line, 4 TYPES OF, is smallest, and the white words have lower contrast on the pale teal. The wording largely repeats the title, adding only the number four.
colors: A flat mint-teal ground with black and white letters, and a maroon blouse and white coat in the photo. Nothing is red or yellow, so there is no danger colour and the palette is calm and clinical.
psychology: A relaxed closed-mouth smile and a direct look at the camera, plus the stethoscope and white coat, read as friendly clinical authority. Nothing in the image signals fear or urgency.
partnership: The title says to say no to these medications; the thumbnail repeats the idea and adds the count of four types. It leaves open which medications, and the soft smile does not dramatise the avoid message.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the woman's face first, then the white word AVOID, then the other lines of text, with 4 TYPES OF read last.
art: A real-looking portrait photo with soft background blur, placed in a rounded frame on a flat colour, like a template or stock layout. The type is plain and the lines are unevenly spaced; there is no compositing artefact.
strength: A real portrait in a white coat with a stethoscope gives an immediate medical-authority cue.
weakness: White words on pale teal are low-contrast, and the five lines are evenly sized with uneven spacing, so no single phrase dominates.
bottleneck: The calm smile and flat teal background carry no tension, so the warning in AVOID has to do all of the work.
action: Hypothesis: set AVOID in black on a solid red or yellow box and recolour the other lines to one dark colour to test whether a single high-contrast warning word draws the eye first.
mechanism: A smiling woman in a white coat with a stethoscope puts a medical-authority face beside a list-style warning about drugs and memory.
mechanism_secondary: numbered list of medications to avoid
counterexample: Seq 7 uses a warning-red background, a pointing hand and a glowing heart for the same kind of authority, while this frame stays calm and flat.
medical_notes: The packaging tells viewers to avoid unspecified drug types and shows a white coat and stethoscope with no printed credential or name, so the safety of the claim cannot be judged from title and image alone.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: FIT, / HEALTHY / & DYING! / THE HIDDEN HEART ATTACK
scene: At right, a bald-topped older man with a grey stubble beard and raised brows looks at the camera with a slightly open mouth. He wears a white coat over teal scrubs, points one finger across his body, and holds a large glowing red anatomical heart with a white crack line in his other hand. A red arrow with a white outline starts beneath the headline's ampersand and points down-right at that pointing finger.
composition: The headline stack takes the left 55 percent in three large lines, and the man's face and heart fill the right 45 percent. A purple banner runs along the bottom edge; his face is at upper right, the heart at lower right, and the arrow connects the headline column to his pointing finger.
typography: Seven words in three tiers: FIT in white, HEALTHY and DYING in yellow-orange gradient capitals with glow, and a white banner line on purple at the bottom. HEALTHY and DYING are huge and clear at 160x90, but the banner line shrinks to a thin strip. The headline adds 'hidden' and drops the cardiologist and the fatal framing of the title.
colors: A deep purple panel on the left and an orange-to-red gradient behind the man, with yellow-gold lettering and a glowing red heart. The reds and orange behind the man and the red arrow signal alarm, and the yellow text has the highest contrast against the purple.
psychology: Raised brows, wide open eyes and a slightly parted mouth read as alarm, and the pointing finger and the glowing cracked heart intensify it. The white coat and scrubs add a medical-authority cue, and the word DYING adds explicit fear.
partnership: The title says a cardiologist warns that healthy people die of heart attacks; the thumbnail compresses this into 'fit, healthy and dying' and adds 'hidden', raising the stakes beyond the title. The glowing heart shows the organ but no cause, leaving the reveal to the video.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: HEALTHY and DYING first, then the man's face, then the glowing heart, then the arrow and finger, and finally the banner line.
art: Polished studio-style composite with heavy glow on the lettering and the heart, and a gradient-lit cutout of the man against the red. The heart is rendered with realistic vessels and a bright crack, and the man's hands and the heart sit coherently in the same lighting.
strength: Huge yellow HEALTHY and DYING beside a cracked glowing heart sets up a stark and instantly legible contradiction.
weakness: The heavy glow, three text tiers, red arrow and gradient background pack a lot of effects into one frame.
bottleneck: The banner line is thin and low-priority at phone size, so the 'hidden' angle that distinguishes the thumbnail from the title is the least visible text.
action: Hypothesis: move THE HIDDEN HEART ATTACK into the main headline stack and drop the red arrow to test whether the added 'hidden' hook works better at headline weight.
mechanism: A doctor-styled man with an alarmed look holds a cracked, glowing heart while the headline puts 'healthy' next to 'dying', making a fear-and-contradiction pairing.
counterexample: Seq 6 puts a smiling doctor on a calm teal ground, so it carries none of this frame's alarm and has no danger colour.
expression_label: raised brows, wide eyes, parted mouth
medical_notes: The packaging pairs the word DYING with a glowing cracked heart and a coat-and-scrubs figure with no printed credential, which dramatises risk beyond what title and image can support.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon figure with a white face, brown messy hair, round black glasses, grey hoodie and black trousers stands at left on a cracked pavement with one hand on his head and a flat, slightly downturned mouth. Behind him is a peeling pale-green house with a broken window, and at right a glossy blue supercar has a big red bow on its roof and a gift tag on its door. Two faces look out from the doorway of the next house and one person stands on a porch at far right.
composition: The figure sits at left of centre at about two thirds of the frame height and the blue car occupies the right half, both on a diagonal sidewalk that leads the eye from bottom left to the car. The peeling house forms the backdrop, and the three onlookers sit small at the upper right.
typography: No text is visible anywhere in the image, so nothing from the title is repeated and the picture has to carry the idea alone.
colors: Washed-out greens, greys and browns for the neighbourhood, against a saturated blue car with a bright red bow. The blue and red together are by far the loudest colours and pull the eye to the car, away from the grey figure.
psychology: The raised hand on the head and the flat, downturned mouth read as bewildered. The staring neighbours add social attention, and the red gift bow signals a surprise, not danger.
partnership: The title asks what it is like to be a trillionaire's family member; the image shows a gifted supercar in a poor street and never shows a trillionaire or a family. It adds a scenario, sudden wealth amid poverty, that the title does not state.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the blue car and red bow first, then the figure's confused face, then the peeling house and neighbours, and last the cracked sidewalk.
art: Hand-inked cartoon with detailed textures on peeling paint, cracks and rust, and a glossy blue car with consistent highlights. The detail-heavy scene is coherent, and the figure's blank white face matches a simple-character style.
strength: A gift-bowed blue car on a decayed street makes the wealth contrast readable without text.
weakness: The figure is a muted grey on a muted background, and the title's trillionaire and family are absent from the image.
bottleneck: With no text and many small background details, only the car and figure survive at phone size, and nothing in the frame signals a trillionaire or a family.
action: Hypothesis: add a short caption such as a dollar figure above the car to test whether naming the wealth is clearer than the unlabelled gift scene.
mechanism: A glossy gift-wrapped supercar parked in front of a run-down house stages the title's wealth-versus-surroundings contrast without a single word.
mechanism_secondary: gift supercar in a poor street
counterexample: Seq 21 is also a text-free single-figure scene, but with a plain grey room and a dim palette, so it has no object as striking as this car.
expression_label: hand on head, flat downturned mouth
hero_object: blue supercar with a red bow
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Five cartoon people stand shoulder to shoulder along the bottom, drawn as exaggerated caricatures. From the viewer's left: a curly-haired man in a light-blue and white striped shirt with a worried look; a man with a black moustache, dark suit, red tie and a gold-and-green chain; a woman with long dark hair, yellow eyes and a green tank top lettered BRASIL; a figure in a multicoloured knitted hat and red poncho with bulging eyes and a wide-open screaming mouth; and a man with curly dark hair, a thick moustache and an orange collared shirt.
composition: The headline spans the full top edge, and the five heads form a nearly even row across the lower two thirds, with the woman at the centre slightly higher than the others. Cropping at the chest keeps every face visible, and the faces overlap their neighbours' shoulders, leaving almost no empty space.
typography: Two words in huge black capitals with a thin white outline fill the whole top edge, the highest-contrast element and fully legible at 160x90. The only other text is the BRASIL lettering partly cut off at the bottom of the green top. The headline omits the title's number twelve and the word stereotypes.
colors: A white ground under black type, with strongly saturated flesh tones, a green-and-yellow tank top, a red tie and a bright orange shirt. The row reads as a wide spread of clothing colours with no single dominant hue, and the black headline outweighs them all.
psychology: The expressions vary from a furrowed worried look through a stern frown and a pouting stare to a screaming open mouth, so the row carries a mix of tension and comic exaggeration. The wide-eyed scream is the one extreme expression and the most attention-drawing face.
partnership: The title promises an explanation of stereotypes for all twelve countries; the thumbnail names only the continent and shows five people, so it implies the stereotype idea through the caricatures but never states the number or the word. Which stereotype goes with which person is left unexplained.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: SOUTH AMERICA first, then the screaming figure in the knitted hat, then the central woman, then the moustached men at either side.
art: Digitally inked caricature illustration with heavy outlines and glossy shading, cleanly cut out with a white keyline against white. The screaming face is deliberately stretched and the other four are drawn semi-realistically, so the group mixes two levels of exaggeration.
strength: A two-word headline across the full top plus five faces gives a loud, readable gallery at any size.
weakness: Reduced to five exaggerated faces and a continent name, the frame leans on stereotyped caricature without saying which stereotype is being explained.
bottleneck: Nothing in the frame states the count or the 'explained' promise from the title, so the viewer sees a lineup and no question to resolve.
action: Hypothesis: add the number 12 beside the headline and drop two of the faces to test whether a stated count plus larger faces improves clarity over five small ones.
mechanism: A line-up of five contrasting national-costume caricatures under a two-word continent name stages a stereotype gallery that the title promises to explain.
counterexample: Seq 18 shows one cartoon man with two data objects and a short headline, keeping a single focal point where this frame splits attention between five faces.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A stick-bodied figure with wild brown hair and a torn tan tunic holds a long brown-stocked musket with a grey barrel across its body. The wide eyes glance down at the gun, the brows tilt upward and the mouth is open with a pink tongue; a thin grey wisp of smoke curls up from the muzzle. Behind it stand a brown rock face with a dark cave opening, two grey boulders and a blue sky above tan sand and a green grass tuft.
composition: The head sits in the upper middle at about a third of the frame height and the long gun runs diagonally across the lower half, pointing left. The headline is in the top-left corner, and the cave and rocks fill the right edge so the figure is framed against the pale sky.
typography: Two yellow capital words with a black outline sit at the top left, small relative to the frame but sharp against the blue at 160x90. FIRST GUN? repeats the title's subject and drops its 'early humans' and 'invent', which the tunic and cave supply.
colors: A flat saturated blue sky, tan sand, brown rock and a yellow headline create a bright primary-style scheme. The white face and grey gun barrel stay legible against the blue, and no colour reads as a warning.
psychology: Upturned worried brows, wide eyes looking down at the gun and an open mouth read as alarm or surprise. The smoke wisp implies the gun has just fired, which adds tension.
partnership: The headline condenses the title into two words and the image adds the prehistoric figure holding a real musket, which the title does not show. The question of how early humans could have invented it stays open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the face with wide eyes first, then the musket and its smoke, then the yellow FIRST GUN? text, and finally the cave at the right.
art: Flat cartoon with a thick uniform outline and no shading, a simple stick-limbed body and a more detailed musket. The gun is anatomically coherent and the shapes read well at small size.
strength: A worried face above a smoking musket gives one clear action frame that a viewer can parse instantly.
weakness: The headline sits small in a corner and the generic caveman cartoon has no distinguishing detail.
bottleneck: The musket looks like a modern-era flintlock, so it works as a joke but does not signal how early humans might have invented it.
action: Hypothesis: replace the musket with a crude tube-and-powder device to test whether an improvised weapon reads as invention more clearly than a finished firearm.
mechanism: A prehistoric-dressed figure staring at a smoking musket sets an anachronism beside a two-word headline that asks who made the first one.
counterexample: Seq 24 keeps the same caveman-in-a-landscape style but uses a dotted arrow to a distant ledge, giving a clear direction that this frame lacks.
expression_label: wide eyes, raised brows, open mouth
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A stick figure with a round head, sweat drop, side-glancing eyes and a flat mouth stands in the exact middle with both palms turned up in a shrug. At left a tan dog on a leash snarls with open jaws, bared teeth and drool; at right a grey cat arches its back, fluffs its fur and hisses with its mouth open and yellow eyes. Trees frame both sides over a blue sky and green grass.
composition: The figure stands at the exact centre as the divider, with the dog on the left and the cat on the right in a mirrored, symmetric arrangement. The big headline spans the top edge, and the animals, larger than the figure, fill the lower two thirds.
typography: Two words in yellow capitals with a black outline run edge to edge across the top and stay readable at 160x90. WHY FIGHT? leaves out cats and dogs, which the animals themselves supply, so the picture carries the nouns and the text the question.
colors: Bright blue sky, green grass and trees, a tan dog and a grey-brown cat, with the yellow headline as the strongest contrast. Nothing is red, so the aggression comes from the bared teeth and arched back and not from colour.
psychology: The dog's open jaws and the cat's arched back read as hostility, while the stick figure's raised palms and sweat drop read as helpless confusion. Three distinct emotions sit side by side.
partnership: The headline abbreviates the title's question, and the image supplies the two animals the title names. It shows the standoff but not any cause, so the reason stays with the video.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow headline first, then the dog's open jaws at left, then the cat at right, then the central stick figure's shrug.
art: Flat cartoon with a clean outline and soft shading on the animals, whose fur and teeth are drawn in more detail than the minimal stick figure. The mix of styles is consistent in line weight, and the shapes stay clear at small size.
strength: A mirrored dog-and-cat standoff around a shrugging stick figure is legible at any size.
weakness: The figure's side glance and shrug are small and generic compared with the two big animals.

text: NEVER DO / THIS IN THE / MORNING / YOUR BLOOD / WILL THICKEN!
scene: At right, an illustrated older man with swept-back grey hair, rectangular glasses and a trimmed grey beard smiles with visible teeth. composition: The five-line headline takes the left 55 percent in a tall stack, and the man fills the right 40 percent from head to waist. A red box under the last two words ends the stack, and the black background separates the colours cleanly with no other objects.
typography: Ten words in five lines, with the first two lines in yellow, the next two in white and the last line in white on a red box; MORNING and BLOOD are the biggest. The five lines are all legible at 160x90 but fill nearly half the frame. The thumbnail names a blood effect and a morning timing that the title phrases differently.
colors: Black ground, yellow and white lettering and a red label box, with the man's blue gingham shirt as the only cool colour. The red box and high-contrast yellow on black read as alarm, so the palette signals danger while the man's face is pleasant.
psychology: The man has a wide smile and a relaxed stance, which sit awkwardly against a headline about blood thickening. The visible mood is friendly, so the urgency comes only from the text and colours.
partnership: The title says a cardiologist warns of four morning habits triggering heart attacks after 60; the thumbnail instead names one unspecified action and one claim, blood thickening. It adds a mechanism not in the title and shows a glass of water that could suggest what the action is, so it risks implying water is the culprit.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: NEVER DO in yellow first, then the red WILL THICKEN! box, then the smiling man, then the water jug.
art: Polished flat-vector illustration with clean outlines, even lighting and a coherent cutout against black. Jug, glass and shirt pattern are all consistent, and the frame survives at small size, with the figure reading as a cheerful stock illustration.
strength: The command-style stacked headline with a red outcome box is the loudest element and is legible at phone size.
weakness: The smiling, relaxed man pouring water does not match the alarming claim, and the image shows no cardiologist cue even though the title does.
bottleneck: The smile and the glass of water contradict the fear text, so the viewer cannot tell whether the water or something else is the 'this'.
action: Hypothesis: replace the smile with a concerned look and show a different morning object than water to test whether matching the expression and object to the warning clarifies the claim.
mechanism: A command headline and a claim about blood thickening are paired with a smiling man pouring water, so the fear message is stated in text while the picture shows an ordinary morning action.
mechanism_secondary: never-do command with a consequence claim
counterexample: Seq 14 shows a stern, white-coat-style figure with the same black-and-red scheme, so its expression matches the warning that this frame's smile contradicts.
hero_object: man pouring a glass of water
medical_notes: The headline states that a morning action will thicken blood without naming it, pairs it with a water glass and shows no clinician cue even though the title cites a cardiologist.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: STOP WAKING UP / TO PEE AT NIGHT / IT'S NOT YOUR BLADDER [clock display: 3:00 AM]

composition: Text stacks in three lines on the left 60 percent and the man occupies the right 40 percent from head to chest. A red banner under the main headline holds the third line, the clock sits at the bottom left, and the man's red wedge background splits the frame diagonally.
typography: Eleven words in three tiers: the yellow headline in two lines with TO in white, then a white line on a red box. All three tiers are legible at 160x90 and the clock's digits are small but still show. The text names a symptom and a cause that the title leaves out, since the title is about how to drink water.
colors: A black field with yellow headline text, a vivid red wedge behind the man, a red label bar and a red-lit clock, with teal scrubs as the one cool accent. Red repeats on three separate objects and signals alarm, and the teal scrubs separate the man from the red.
psychology: Furrowed brows, a closed straight mouth and a direct stare read as serious and stern. The red clock and red panel add urgency, and the glass of water in his hand is a calm counterpoint.
partnership: The title is a how-to about drinking water after 60 to avoid waking at night; the thumbnail leads with a stop command and a cause claim that the title lacks. The water glass links to the title, and the 3:00 AM clock shows the problem, but the thumbnail implies a diagnosis that the title does not.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: STOP WAKING UP in yellow first, then the man's stern face, then the red IT'S NOT YOUR BLADDER banner, and finally the 3:00 AM clock.
art: Studio-style composite with a cutout of the man against a flat red wedge, a glowing red clock with a soft reflection and a glass of water with believable highlights. The man's real-looking photo styling contrasts with the pure flat text boxes, and the lighting on the glass and the face is consistent.
strength: The 3:00 AM clock shows the exact problem in one object and ties the headline to a specific moment.
weakness: The thumbnail denies the bladder explanation without showing what is the cause, and the red repeats on three objects.
bottleneck: The cause claim is the strongest hook but also the most medically loaded line, and it sits in a small banner below the main headline.
action: Hypothesis: show the water glass larger and the clock smaller to test whether the how-to element from the title earns more visual weight than the diagnosis line.
mechanism: A clock showing 3:00 AM and a stern clinician-styled man holding water place the night-waking problem and a reassurance-by-contradiction line, 'it's not your bladder', in one frame.
mechanism_secondary: symptom plus denied cause with a 3:00 AM clock
counterexample: Seq 6 uses a pale teal ground and a smiling woman in a white coat with no red, so it has none of this frame's urgency colours.
expression_label: furrowed brows, closed straight mouth, direct stare
medical_notes: The line 'it's not your bladder' reads as a diagnostic statement, and the scrubs and stethoscope carry no printed name or credential, so the claim needs the video's evidence.
